title: Conditionals check
instructions: Five questions on if, elif and else.

questions.prompt: With x = 5, the chain is: if x > 3 prints a, elif x > 1 prints b, else prints c. What is printed?
questions.explanation: Only the first true branch runs. x > 3 is true, so a is printed and the rest are skipped.
An empty list counts as False. A list with any item, even [0], counts as True.

questions.prompt: Which line is a mistake when you want to check whether x is 5?
questions.explanation: A single = assigns, so this is a SyntaxError. Comparing uses ==.

questions.prompt: score = 95. The chain first checks `if score >= 70` (sets C) and only then `elif score >= 90` (sets A). What does it set?
questions.explanation: 95 is at least 70, so the first branch wins and the A branch is never reached. Check the strictest condition first.

questions.prompt: What must come right after an if line, which ends with a colon?
questions.explanation: The indented lines are the body. Python uses indentation to know which lines belong to the if.

title: Grade and parity
instructions:
`score` and `number` are set for you.

1. Create `grade` from `score` using `if`, `elif` and `else`: 90 or more is `"A"`, 80 or more is `"B"`, 70 or more is `"C"`, anything lower is `"F"`.
2. Create `parity`: `"even"` if `number` is even, otherwise `"odd"`.
3. Print `grade`, then print `parity` on the next line.
starter_code:
score = 80
number = 7

# Create grade and parity, then print both

tests.description: grade is B for a score of exactly 80
the program prints B and then odd
